items.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
items.summary: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. items.summary: Successful tool-use trajectories are not necessarily useful supervision. items.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
items.summary: Vision-language models are shifting from offline passive understanding toward online proactive interaction. items.title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
items.summary: LLM agents are increasingly used to solve real-world problems, and their effectiveness depends on both the underlying models and the harnesses that support their operation. items.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
items.summary: People have long dreamed of an assistant that is always there to guide them and remind what they forget, from new dishes to lost keys. items.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
items.summary: Multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse task requirements. items.summary: Precise camera control is essential for cinematic character video generation, yet existing methods struggle to follow large-angle trajectories with combined rotation, translation, and radius variation from arbitrary initial azimuths. items.title: Function-Space Temporal Self-Distillation for Policy Optimization
items.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) improves reasoning in language models, but scalar outcomes provide coarse supervision over response trajectories. items.summary: Spatial audio authoring coordinates source decisions with soundfield synthesis. items.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
items.summary: As foundation models evolve from information generation to digital work execution, agents are increasingly capable of completing complex tasks across tools, applications, and workflows. items.title: Eat Your Precision: Precision Objective Mitigates Reward Hacking in Rubric-based RL
items.summary: Rubric-based rewards enable effective reinforcement learning on non-verifiable tasks. However, because these rewards are typically defined as a weighted measure of rubric coverage, models are trained primarily to maximize a recall objective. items.title: World-in-Context: Interactive Video World Modeling with In-Context Conditioning
items.summary: Interactive video world models require coordinated control over viewing perspectives, character actions, and camera motion. items.summary: Behavior cloning for robotic manipulation is highly sensitive to the coverage of its training data, yet collecting diverse successful demonstrations remains costly. items.summary: Learning visual design is essential for prompt enhancement (PE) to turn underspecified user requests into coherent visual specifications for text-to-image (T2I) generation. items.summary: Scientific discovery requires identifying the scientific principles underlying observed phenomena to guide further investigation. items.title: Δτ-Bench: Pushing Agents Toward a Moving Capability
items.summary: In this paper, we introduce Δτ-Bench, an executable agent benchmark that models the structural evolution of large tool ecosystems. items.title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
items.summary: Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long time horizons, yet current evaluations largely assess individual task performance rather than improvement through accumulated experience. items.summary: Critic-free methods are widely used in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, avoiding difficult and costly critic training. items.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
items.summary: AI systems built around large models increasingly use experience and feedback to make persistent changes to models, prompts, memories, tools, and workflows. items.summary: Scaling vision-language-action (VLA) models is constrained by scarce action-labeled demonstrations and incompatible control spaces across robot embodiments. items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as the primary paradigm for optimizing Large Language Model (LLM) agents, yet efficient critic-free algorithms (e.g., GRPO) suffer from a fundamental uniform credit assignment dilemma that broadcasts trajectory-level advantages equally to all actions. items.summary: Can LLM agents carry a hard real-world problem from raw data to a system that holds its own against people? items.summary: Large-scale AI training increasingly relies on massive video datasets with random temporal sampling patterns. items.summary: When humans collaborate with AI agents on long-horizon tasks, what happens to the agents' contributions?
